source.document: Guglieri López B. Population Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacodynamic Modelling to Optimize Lenalidomide Treatment in Multiple Myeloma Patients. Doctoral thesis, Universitat de València, March 2017 (directors: Merino Sanjuán M, Porta Oltra B, Climente Martí M).

file_reviewed.file: 40e68fca-34579.pdf (265 pages, text layer; title metadata 'Tesis Beatriz Guglieri Lopez 12032017 v11')

source.storage: Supplied by the platform owner; kept on the owner's computer, not committed.
source.extraction: AI-assisted. Every quote in this file was checked against text extracted from the thesis (pdftotext; line breaks and soft hyphens normalised to single spaces), and every table value against the same text. Independent review pending.
source.publication_status: Whether the PK/PD analyses were published in a peer-reviewed journal was not checked.

design.setting: Observational, prospective, non-controlled study in routine clinical practice at one centre (Doctor Peset University Hospital, Valencia, Spain), January 2014 to August 2016
design.population: Adults with active multiple myeloma on lenalidomide with dexamethasone, mostly as second or later line; two patients first line
design.regimen: Lenalidomide 25 mg on days 1-21 of 28-day cycles, adjusted for renal impairment per the label and for grade 3/4 toxicity; dexamethasone 40 mg (20 mg at age 75 or over) weekly
design.exposure_definition: AUC0-inf and Cmax per dose from the author's population PK model: individual (Bayesian) estimates for the 15 sampled patients, typical values from dose history and covariates for the rest; used as a time-varying covariate

inclusion.quote: Treated with lenalidomide (Revlimid®) in combination with dexamethasone at any dose level at the moment of inclusion.

pk_subgroup.quote: Blood samples could only be obtained in 15 patients.

population_predicted.quote: the population pharmacokinetic parameters obtained from the selected PK model were used for more than half of the patients included in the study (65%).

time_varying.quote: Exposure was then used as a time-varying covariate, thus longitudinal lenalidomide exposure was evaluated as a risk factor of disease progression or severe neutropenia.

prior_treatment_required.quote: At least one month receiving lenalidomide

design.time_zero: Time to progression counted from the start of lenalidomide (section 6.4.1, PDF pages 214-215), while patients were enrolled after at least one month on it

time_to_progression.model: Parametric time-to-event, log-normal baseline hazard; covariates on the hazard
time_to_progression.location: Section 5.3.2.1, Table 5.17 (PDF page 193); NONMEM code PDF page 249

hazard_ratios.covariate: autologous stem cell transplantation before lenalidomide

hazard_ratios.unit: IgA, light-chain or non-secretory vs IgG
per 100 ug.h/L increase above 1,110 ug.h/L (none below)

time_to_progression.auc_threshold_basis: Median AUC0-inf of the sample (thesis section 6.4.1); hinge form IF(AUC.GT.1110) in the NONMEM code
time_to_progression.direction: Higher exposure was associated with a higher hazard of progression, i.e. shorter time to progression.

events.quote: A total of 26 events (24 progressions and 2 deaths due to progression) were recorded in the 54 patients included for this analysis.

result.quote: patients with lenalidomide AUC0-∞ above 1,110 µg·h/L (median value of the studied sample) had an increased risk of disease progression of 19.7% per each 100 µg·h/L increase of AUC0-∞ (Table 5.17).

author_caution.quote: Nevertheless, the confidence interval for the effect of AUC0-∞ on the risk of progression was close to one (HR=1.19 95%CI 1.08- 1.35), and thus results should be interpreted carefully.

time_to_severe_neutropenia.model: Parametric time-to-event, exponential baseline hazard; covariates on the hazard
time_to_severe_neutropenia.auc_tested_not_retained: AUC0-inf was not significant in the univariate analysis (dOFV -0.746, p = 0.387; Table 5.19, PDF page 199)

events.quote: A total of 27 patients experienced severe neutropenia during lenalidomide treatment.

result.quote: Finally, the risk of experiencing severe neutropenia increased by 2% per each 10 ng/mL increase of lenalidomide Cmax.

platform_assessment.recorded_by: AI-assisted review, 31 October 2026; not the author's view
platform_assessment.use_on_platform: Shown as a cited finding only. Not used in any calculation, and no dose-level hazard is derived from it.
reasons: Exposure is largely dose history: for 65% of patients it is a typical value computed from dose and covariates, so the analysis cannot separate exposure from the doses that clinicians chose.

Doses in routine practice are reduced for toxicity, renal function and over time, so who keeps a high dose is not random; a time-varying exposure covariate under these conditions is open to confounding and reverse causation. The thesis does not report an analysis addressing this.

Patients entered the study only after at least one month on lenalidomide, but time was counted from its start, so early progressions before enrolment could not be observed (prevalent-user design); the thesis does not report a correction.
54 patients and 26 events at one centre; the AUC threshold is the sample median, chosen from the same data.
The direction (more exposure, faster progression) is opposite to the usual expectation; the author proposes acquired resistance as an explanation, which the data do not test.
The neutropenia result concerns Cmax, not AUC (AUC was not significant), with a hazard ratio of 1.02 per 10 ng/mL and lenalidomide given with dexamethasone.

not_this: Not evidence that a lower dose is more effective.
